utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have all the situation reports that we generated at that time so I don't know where it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, as a soldier, do you make a distinction between operative, tactical, and strategic levels? You, Major Nikolic, are you the level that decides on such matters?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, ours was not to make decisions on any matter. It was to convey decisions made at higher levels in our own areas. On my side, through the UN system all the way from the top, and on Major Nikolic or Colonel Vukovic's side, all the way through the military leadership up to the civilian leadership of the country, because for sure it was not a military leadership. It was a civilian-led leadership. So the decisions -- no, the -- what was being conveyed by Major Nikolic or Colonel Vukovic obviously we expected to be coming from somewhere up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, your expectation was wrong. Look at paragraph 31. Vukovic said to you, [In English] "We should tell -- go and tell ..." [Interpretation] It was the conditional, wasn't it? Paragraph 31. [In English] "We should tell -- go and tell the Muslims to pack up and leave Srebrenica." [Interpretation] But what the problem with your statement is analogies and conclusions in keeping --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- with your own wishes, wishful thinking. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: He start -- he asked a question. He didn't wait for the answer. Then he made another statement by saying: "But what the problem with your statement is analogies and conclusions in keeping --" he would just have continued again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: -- with his statements unless stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I had enough time I would deal with each and every paragraph, and I will ask for each and every paragraph that I had not dealt with in cross-examination not to be taken into account or that I be given enough time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for you, Mr. Kingori, please look at paragraph 31, does it not say this in the conditional, "we should ..." et cetera?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, what is mentioned in paragraph 31 is very true. That is what he told us and that is what he meant. And as I said earlier, we went on to believe that he meant it because that is exactly what was done by the BSA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know, Mr. Kingori, that the United Nations and the Muslim side already on the 10th knew that the Serbs do not have a decision to the effect that they would enter Srebrenica. On the 10th of July the Serbs do not intend to go into Srebrenica yet and all the intercepts and all the reports show that. The Serbs entered Srebrenica because the 28th Division had left Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the aim of starting the war on Srebrenica had to have -- I mean was there from the beginning and it's qualified by what I've just quoted from Colonel Vukovic, and which I said was actually conveying a message from a higher up. Secondly, the BSA really had to get into the enclave. The fact that their conversations that they were not going in or they were going in, or they were going, or whatever, really does not arise because immediately after they softened the target, immediately after they had hit the area so hard that it was very soft now, they went in through the normal way, that is, with the infantry. And I've quoted that in -- you know, somewhere in here. They had to bring in the infantry to mop-up the place, to clear the place, and that's exactly what they did. So the intention must have been there from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know what the intention of the Serb army was? How did you get to that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I will say it again, it was conveyed to us by Colonel Vukovic and also initially by Major Nikolic, and we went on to believe it was true because that is exactly what happened. I think this could be the third or fourth time I'm repeating it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. -- just a second --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, your time is up. But how much would you need for your re-examination, Ms. West?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll only need five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask for more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long would you need to wrap-up your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, at least an additional session. This kind of witness, with over 200 paragraphs, with generalised statements, if the Chamber is going to take into account any one of these statements, I ask for the opportunity to challenge them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Make your questions simpler and be focused in putting your question. You'll have an hour tomorrow morning in addition to today's session.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Just one matter. As you're aware, tomorrow we have two DutchBat witnesses who are testifying in Dutch, and so tomorrow the Dutch interpreters have been ordered. I understand that their testimony probably in total would be four hours. We have been rescheduling this a few times because of the issue of the interpreters, so I wonder if you could take that into account so that we don't have them go over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you mean that hearing the -- one of the DutchBat officers next week is impossible? I was not informed of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I think -- well, of course it's not -- anything is possible, but I would wonder if perhaps tomorrow morning we could start with the DutchBat officers because they've been rescheduled so many times and we specifically have Dutch interpreters here tomorrow. I don't know, I wonder if Mr. Kingori could then testify, and if it goes over, then he goes over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll have to clarify with Mr. Kingori, whether he has any problem staying over in the weekend until -- staying until next Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have some domestic problems because I had not made some arrangements at home that I will stay longer than eight days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll sort out after today's hearing is adjourned in co-operation with the Registry. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at your paragraph 32 in your statement. First of all, up here we have this conditional phrase and then in paragraph 32 you take this to be an official document and then you give your own judgement. Just take a look at paragraph 32, isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is -- actually, taken from what Colonel Vukovic had said and I've just summarised and said it was not just a threat. Initially we thought it was just a threat and we conveyed the same, even to the Muslims, but later on it was actualised and that is exactly what I've said here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, by "conditional phrase," what did you refer to in his amalgamated statement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in paragraph 31, Mr. Kingori remembered that Colonel Vukovic said "we should say" and in our language that would be the conditional, like it would allow for the possibility of us sending them that message. It's like when someone says "I'd kill him" and then no one kills anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what do you say -- actually, do you know how many Serbs lived in Srebrenica before 1992? We can just have a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I tell you that one-third of the population and at least one-third of the villages were Serb and that none of that existed any longer after May 1992 already, they were all killed or expelled, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that throughout Republika Srpska, then and today, there were Muslims who lived in towns and villages with a Serb majority population?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your conclusion is that Serbs planned, said, asked for Muslim civilians to be evacuated from the enclave, and this is what I put to you. The Muslim government in Srebrenica and the Muslim government in Sarajevo and your commands and the United Nations and the envoy of the Secretary-General and Mr. Karremans, all of you were planning for them to leave and only the Serb side was silent awaiting what the Muslim side had to say?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I know is that the UN did not have any such plans. What I said or what I wrote was part of what was told to us by Colonel Vukovic, a BSA officer, and Major Nikolic, also from BSA. So I do not know what else to add on that because it was not coming from myself as Colonel Kingori or from the UN system. It was coming from your [Realtime transcript read in error "the"] officers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 01883 would be the 65 ter number that I'd like to have displayed now. I think it's been admitted recently as a P document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4150, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe before you start on that the answer that I gave, the last part, I said it was coming from "your officers" not from "the officers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kingori.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who else? Who were the other officers in addition to the ones that you've already mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are several other officers that we were meeting with and the names are somewhere within the reports that we made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said in this paragraph here and during your examination-in-chief, I think, that in addition to these two there were six high-ranking officers attending the meeting with you. Who are they?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't remember their names, but they were names like Dricic [phoen] and several other officers. Right now I cannot remember the names offhand. But we listed the names and we gave them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Today you said not only from the army. Tell us, who was there on behalf of the government, the civilian authorities, who had these plans and how were you assured of that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I knew at that time is that there was a civilian government in place in Sarajevo for the whole of Bosnia that was -- that had an army that we were calling the BSA which was led by General Mladic and which had hierarchy all the way down, up to the lowest level that we were operating with, that was Colonel Vukovic and Major Nikolic, and the civilian leadership was in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Today you implied that you had proof that it wasn't only these two local officers, middle-ranking, that had this intention, but there were others who shared that intention at higher levels too. Tell us, do you have proof of that? Do you have names? And then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I said that, I cannot remember. What I know is that these officers were conveying messages given to them, obviously, from higher up in the hierarchy, in the leadership, all the way down to that level. And even on our side we were giving information that we had from up there and the opposite is also true, that whatever we got from there, the officers we were calling middle-ranking officers, we had to take it all the way up to the UN system. And that if there was anything to be discussed at other higher levels, at the general level or at the presidential level, it would be done at their own level, not at ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're speculating, Mr. Kingori. Do you have proof or are you just speculating, drawing logical conclusions, or do you have proof in actual fact?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not speculation. Your Honour, there is -- there was a special -- a proper chain of command all the way for the BSA. There was a chain of command. All the way from the lowest to the highest level --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are logical conclusions. Do you have any proof --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, he is spending my time in dealing with general questions that I never put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are just repeating your question on the topic to which the witness has already answered. It's time to adjourn for today --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just introduce this document, Excellency, the one that we've already seen? I hope that everybody saw that. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we've had this document called up, I would like to present it, introduce it, to show how these Muslim structures --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- started with these requests for having the population evacuated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you didn't ask a question about this. Please carry on. What is your question? I take it the witness has read this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, in this text by Mr. Akashi it says that it was the initiative of the Muslim government - and this was written on the 11th in the morning - to organise discussions with the Serbian side in order to evacuate civilians from Srebrenica. And before that, on the 9th July, the same initiative is expressed by the Muslim authorities of Srebrenica. They request from the Serbian side to open a corridor so that the population can leave for the nearest free territory. And already on the 11th Akashi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- describes all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- are you asking a question about Mr. Akashi's report or on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I am going to introduce Akashi's report, not today but tomorrow. I'm asking if Mr. Kingori knows that this initiative of the 9th came from the Muslim authorities of Srebrenica, that the population be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the question, whether you knew that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The initiative of the 9th came from Muslim authorities of Srebrenica, that the population be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can see that report here, that request, but this cannot be dealt with in isolation because the activities which were going on there meant the Muslims had to get out of Srebrenica. It reached a point where they were taken all the way to Potocari, living in very bad conditions, and so we had also even requested that they be evacuated. So the evacuation, even if it originated or there was a letter to that effect, I'm sure the BSA maybe did not know about it at that particular moment. But they went ahead and evacuated or removed the Muslims from there using their own buses, as we have already seen and as it is in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Court Deputy approach the bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I just had a word with the Court Deputy and was confirmed that we can continue with Mr. Kingori's evidence tomorrow morning. We'll adjourn for today and resume at 9.00 -- but before that, yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Apologies, Mr. President. I just wanted to alert you that last time with the Dutch interpreters in December, we had difficulty getting them for another day, and I just wondered if perhaps tomorrow we might consider going long if there was an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was informed that they will be available on Monday as well. Just one quick matter. I appreciate the indulgence of the staff members, but I was informed that Defence filed a motion to exclude some part of evidence from Mr. Tucker's statement which was filed today and I wonder whether we can have your response by the end of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 13th day of January, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.07 p.m.,
